evidence.quote: In comparison to the Brass-filled PTFE, a similar metal filled PTFE compound named Salox-M® uses Bronze filler in PTFE instead of Brass.
The composition of Salox-M® is 40% Bronze and 60% PTFE.

explanation: The source describes Salox-M® as a metal filled PTFE compound.
Salox-M® contains PTFE as a component.
The reported share of PTFE in Salox-M® is 60% on a basis the source does not state.
Status: SOURCE_SUPPORTED_PENDING_REVIEW; relation hasComponent is a staged proposal, not approved vocabulary; source page 10.

evidence.quote: The scientists and engineers at the Materials Combustion Research Facility, in cooperation with seal suppliers, are currently testing a new formulation of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) with Brass filler.
Although the percentage of Brass in the Brass-filled PTFE is not known, it can be determined from figures 1 and 2 that it is far less than 40%.
This Brass-filled PTFE is showing great promise as a seal and seat material for high-pressure oxygen systems.

explanation: Brass-filled PTFE contains Brass as a component.
Brass acts as the filler of Brass-filled PTFE, in polytetrafluoroethylene.
The source states that the share of Brass in Brass-filled PTFE is not known.
Status: SOURCE_SUPPORTED_PENDING_REVIEW; relation hasComponent is a staged proposal, not approved vocabulary; source page 2, 10.

assertion_characteristics.context: The material in which a nested component is described (the bronze of one formulation).
assertion_characteristics.proportion: The documented share of the component, with its documented basis (mass, volume, molar) or UNSPECIFIED_IN_SOURCE.
assertion_characteristics.role: The component's documented function in this material (e.g. filler); a characteristic of one assertion, not a global property.

ontology_extension_proposals.definition: The subject material contains the object material as a constituent, as the source states.
ontology_extension_proposals.why_existing_relations_do_not_fit: madeOf relates a sample, run or experiment family to its material; no approved relation links a material to its constituents.
